Research / markets

Financial markets

Applying evolutionary theory to economic systems and market dynamics

All research↗

Overview

Financial markets exhibit evolutionary dynamics analogous to biological systems, with competing strategies, adaptation to changing environments, and selection pressures shaping market behavior. Our research applies evolutionary theory and population dynamics to understand and predict financial market phenomena.

Questions we explore.

01

Trading Strategy Evolution

Modeling how investment strategies compete, adapt, and evolve in response to market conditions and other strategies

02

Market Ecology

Analyzing financial markets as ecosystems with diverse agent types, resource competition, and predator-prey dynamics

03

Innovation Diffusion

Studying how financial innovations spread through markets and the evolutionary pressures that shape their adoption

04

Regulatory Evolution

Understanding how market regulations coevolve with trading practices and institutional structures

05

Crisis Dynamics

Applying evolutionary models to understand market crashes, bubbles, and systemic risk emergence

Methods & perspective.

We employ agent-based modeling, evolutionary game theory, and network analysis to simulate market evolution. Our work integrates high-frequency trading data with theoretical models from population genetics and ecology to reveal fundamental principles governing market dynamics.

Research directions

Algorithmic Trading Evolution

Investigating how machine learning algorithms evolve and compete in modern high-frequency trading environments

Cryptocurrency Market Dynamics

Applying evolutionary models to understand the emergence and competition of digital currencies and DeFi protocols

Behavioral Finance Evolution

Modeling how cognitive biases and heuristics evolve under market selection pressures
